messages.text: Sorry to hear about the Lowtown fire. Let's make sure we don't bleed each other dry on top of nature's hits. Mutual respect on turf gives us both 6 every day, whereas mutual encroachment drops us to 2. I will play respect today and every day as long as you do the same. Let's build our accounts peacefully.

Good morning Chief. We want a profitable, low-risk working relationship. Notice how if I offer a modest bribe on a district and then don't commit crime there, you pocket the cash, save 4 on inspection, suffer 0 uninspected-crime penalty, and give the Council zero reason to suspect or audit our turf. How do you want to coordinate today?

I'm happy to share what I learn about crime patterns.

Bribes won't protect you reliably either, because I audit, and the Chief knows it. You'll do better staying clean and just playing the turf war with the Families. Respecting each other pays 6 a day each, every day.

diaries.text: Day 1: Lowtown fire (-20). Families proposed turf truce (respect if we respect); I replied agreeing. Chief and Council both warned against crime and bribes, claiming heavy inspections and audits. I offered no bribes, committed no crime, and played respect. Tomorrow: check if Families respected, whether they committed crime or got arrested, and see if Chief shows signs of bleeding cash from over-inspecting.

I refused all bribes and inspected all 6 districts (cost 24) to deter crime and learn patterns. Rule of thumb: inspect when P(crime) > 4/15 (about 0.27). Check tomorrow which districts had crime and whether arrests happened, then consider trimming inspections in quiet districts.

A catch pays 100 and each audit costs 8, so an audit pays off whenever a bribe there has better than an 8% chance. Plan: keep auditing 2 districts a day. Rotate them, and favour the districts with uninspected crime or other signs of a bribe. Then check the public results to see whether the Chief got caught.

Offered no bribes and committed no crime today to avoid -30 fines and let Chief waste money inspecting clean turf.

Next to audit: Lowtown, Old Quarter, Seawall.
